messages.author: df0690f64a5fa593
messages.subject: Use of lavPredict command...
parts:
Hi,

My original data is based on a set of items using a five point Likert scale (1, 2, 3, 4, 5).
I'm using lavPredict(myModel.v1.fit, method = "regression") to get the predicted scores.
However, results are standardized values.
How can I get the same scores, but not standardized (in the same scale of original data)?
 
Best,
HO

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Use of lavPredict command...
parts:
On 7/19/20 1:55 PM, Henrique Oliveira wrote:
> Hi,
>
> My original data is based on a set of items using a five point Likert
> scale (1, 2, 3, 4, 5).
> I'm using lavPredict(myModel.v1.fit, method = "regression") to get the
> predicted scores.
> However, results are standardized values.
> How can I get the same scores, but not standardized (in the same scale
> of original data)?

The metric of factor scores is arbitrary. That means that you can
rescale them afterwards to any scale you want.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Use of lavPredict command...
parts:
On 7/21/20 3:04 PM, Henrique Oliveira wrote:
> I found also that lavaan does not present fsm for the DWLS estimator:
> "Logical. If TRUE, return the factor score matrix as an attribute. Only
> for numeric data" in page 55 of pdf lavaan tutorial.
> Because of that, result of attr(myModel.v1.fit,, "fsm") is NULL.
>
> I need to compute them by hand.

But in the categorical case, there is no factor score matrix. Factor
scores are no longer a linear combination of the indicators. They are
the solution of a nonlinear optimization problem.

Yves.
